Baseline sweep found 32 violations across 22 files in 9 packages, all repaired the #10120 way (module-top side-effect import); one cli file's redundant 60s beforeAll warm-up was removed with it. Status is rework, not done, because layer 4 (the convention sentence in AGENTS.md's testing conventions) is BLOCKED: AGENTS.md sits exactly on its shrink-only line ceiling (958, headroom 0), the mandated sentence costs +3 lines, and its own section has 2 lines of lossless rewrap headroom — see open_questions.   "open_questions": [
    {
      "question": "Layer 4: where does the convention sentence live? AGENTS.md is capped at 958 lines by scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs and origin/main is at exactly 958 (headroom 0). The maintainer-specified sentence — 'clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading — a test that boots a real plugin chain pays its first load at module top' — is 122 characters, so at the file's 90-column fill it costs 2 prose lines plus a blank: +3. Measured lossless rewrap headroom in the whole section it would join: 2 lines (type-check paragraph 7->6, the @ts-expect-error bullet 8->7); every other paragraph there is already at fill. The ratchet's own remedy is 'compress in place, or a maintainer ruling quoted in the raising PR'. Note the ruling I have (2026-08-20, 「立卡」, accepting layers 1+4) accepts the layer, not a ceiling raise, and was made without the collision in view — quoting it as authority to raise the roof would be exactly the stretch the ratchet exists to refuse.",
      "options": [
        "A — maintainer rules the ceiling to 961 (+3); a one-commit follow-up adds the sentence to AGENTS.md § Build & Test and quotes the ruling in its PR body, per the ratchet's own escape hatch.",
        "B — a separate compression card lowers AGENTS.md by >= 3 lines first (the largest single lossless win in the file is 8 lines in the merge-discipline list around line 400); the sentence then lands inside the existing ceiling with headroom to spare.",
        "C — accept the sentence's current home: verbatim in the gate header AND in the failure text, pinned by a self-test assertion. Every author who trips the rule reads it; AGENTS.md carries nothing. Zero further work, but the convention is not in the binding instruction file.",
        "D — truncate the sentence to fit 1 line (e.g. 'Clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading — pay the first load at module top.', 84 chars, net-zero against the 2 lines of rewrap headroom). Lands today inside the ceiling, but edits a sentence the maintainer specified verbatim."
      ],
      "recommendation": "A, with B as the principled alternative. On real business need: the audience that caused this incident is agents, and agents read AGENTS.md — option C leaves the convention only where someone already failing meets it, which is remediation, not prevention. On long-term soundness: B is the architecturally cleanest (it pays down surface instead of raising a roof) but it makes a P0 remediation wait on an unrelated compression card, and the ratchet explicitly provides A as the sanctioned route for a deliberate protocol addition. On making AI-written code hard to get wrong: the gate already makes the mistake structurally impossible to merge, so the doc line is reinforcement rather than enforcement — which is why A's small, ruled, one-time cost beats D. I recommend against D specifically: silently trimming a maintainer-specified sentence to satisfy a line count is the kind of quiet edit that reads as the maintainer's wording to every later reader."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": []
}

Effect: the `scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` ceiling for AGENTS.md is ruled from 958 to **961** (+3), exactly the cost of the mandated convention sentence at 90-column fill. The follow-up commit adds the sentence — unedited — to AGENTS.md § Build & Test and its PR body quotes this ruling, per the ratchet's own escape hatch ("compress in place, or a maintainer ruling quoted in the raising PR"). This ruling authorizes THIS +3 for THIS sentence only; it is not a general license to raise the ceiling.

Layer ④ is hereby unblocked; dispatching the follow-up to the same dev on the same branch/PR (#10135), which then becomes `Fixes #10126`.
